title: The Benumbed Waves, Everything Is Improving, I Am a Microbe
source: Yevgeny Zamyatin We Record Twenty-Two, Gregory Zilboorg translation 1924; original dialogue and witness reading

scenes.title: 01 · The March That Freezes
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: A million footsteps move together. Then the wave stops.
scenes.story: During the prescribed Walk, the Numbers move like a unified Assyrian army. As they approach the Accumulator Tower, a quadrangle of Guardians with three prisoners blocks their route. The sudden interruption resembles a wave freezing in mid-crest.
scenes.observation: A coordinated public Walk is interrupted by a guarded group of three prisoners.
scenes.inference: The entire city has rebelled because a single procession momentarily stopped.
scenes.question: What was directly observed?
choices: One Walk and one interruption, not a citywide uprising.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.

scenes.title: 02 · Blue Sparks at Thirteen Oh Six
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: A thin young neck rises above the crowd. Then the sparks strike.
scenes.story: At 13:06, a young prisoner stands on tiptoe, apparently scanning the marching crowd. A Guardian repeatedly uses an electric whip on him. D-503 initially admires the instrument as a technological improvement over ancient whips.
scenes.observation: A prisoner is struck repeatedly while D-503 rationalizes the device's appearance.
scenes.inference: Technical sophistication makes deliberate cruelty morally better.
scenes.question: What must the witness distinguish?
choices: The device and the narrator's approval from any justified moral evaluation.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.

scenes.title: 03 · One Woman Breaks the Rows
scenes.speaker: NARRATOR · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: She moves against the ranks and cries for the blows to stop.
scenes.story: A woman abruptly breaks from the synchronized Walk and intervenes to protest the Guardian's treatment of a prisoner. The marching crowd freezes as two Guardians move to capture her.
scenes.observation: An unidentified woman protests and disrupts the procession.
scenes.inference: A single protest immediately reveals every dissident or an organized leader.
scenes.question: What is grounded?
choices: A public intervention, a halt, and a response from Guardians.
The protester's network or full intentions.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.

scenes.title: 04 · The Woman Who Was Not I-330
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: I recognized the movement. I ran. Then I saw her freckles.
scenes.story: D-503 recognizes the protester's distinctive posture as I-330's and races forward to protect her from capture. When she turns, he sees freckles and red brows and realizes she is someone else. His impulse quickly reverses into a desire for her arrest.
scenes.observation: D-503 acts on mistaken recognition and then corrects it on seeing the face.
scenes.inference: His initial certainty was proof of I-330's identity.
scenes.question: What changed the identification?
choices: New facial evidence contradicted his first recognition.
A retroactive erasure of his attempt to help.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.

scenes.title: 05 · A Hand on D-503's Shoulder
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: They have me now. Even my explanation sounds dangerous.
scenes.story: A Guardian restrains D-503 and leads him away. He attempts to explain that he mistook the woman for I-330, but he cannot frame his reasons clearly. He fears the world of glass and blue sky will be taken away from him.
scenes.observation: D-503 is detained and struggles to explain his movement.
scenes.inference: Detention proves a particular charge or final conviction.
scenes.question: What remains open?
choices: What punishment, if any, will follow his detention.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.

scenes.title: 06 · S-4711 Writes a Note
scenes.speaker: S-4711 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: D-503 has been ill. His emotions overcame his discipline.
scenes.story: S-4711 arrives, testifies that D-503 has been ill and attributes his behavior to indignation toward the protester. D-503 claims to have shouted for her arrest; another Guardian contradicts him. He retreats to saying he only intended to shout. S-4711 writes a note and D-503 is released.
scenes.observation: S-4711 offers an exculpatory interpretation; D-503's claim about shouting is corrected; the note enables his release.
scenes.inference: An intended but unspoken shout is an audible act, or release proves innocence.
scenes.question: Which witness correction matters?
choices: D-503 did not shout, although he later claimed he wanted to.
That his account of shouting was accurate.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.

scenes.title: 07 · The Body and the Microbe
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE DIALOGUE
scenes.line: The marching body is whole again. But I am no longer one of its obedient cells.
scenes.story: The Walk resumes. D-503 briefly imagines himself as one harmonious part of a larger social organism, then recognizes that his independent impulses make him resemble the microbes he previously condemned. He pictures I-330 and perhaps thousands of others as hidden dissenters, wondering if this disturbance foreshadows more.
scenes.observation: D-503 reflects on his own dissent and speculates about a larger movement.
scenes.inference: His metaphor identifies thousands of verified rebels or predicts a certain revolution.
scenes.question: What carries into W023?
choices: New self-recognition and the possibility, not proof, of wider unrest.
A confirmed headcount or guaranteed uprising.
reply: Correct: the chapter supports the event without that extra inference.
That conclusion outruns the observed event.
